name: pneumatic-carrier-dispatch
title: Pneumatic Carrier Dispatch
description: A background job/export queue tray drawn as a pneumatic tube transport: a loaded carrier launches on blower pressure, cruises near top speed, then brakes against a trapped air cushion and thunks softly into a shared catch tray, three lanes running staggered on their own clocks.
useWhen: a background job/export/print/sync queue surface where the mechanic should live in the transport itself — a launch, a cruise, a real deceleration before arrival — rather than a plain per-row spinner or percentage bar; pick capstan-slip instead for a single determinate transfer whose mechanic is a constant-speed shaft with a periodic slip, or refresh-pull-flywheel for a one-shot pull-triggered refresh rather than a continuously self-dispatching queue. Distinct from soxhlet-siphon-cycle's single slow-fill/fast-dump chamber and transfer-list-siphon's user-primed one-time drain — this is several independently-timed carriers arriving into an accumulating tray, never a single vessel.
instruction: `<PneumaticCarrierDispatch label? showReadout? className? />` — a card-scale SVG side view of a pneumatic tube dispatch line, ambient and self-driving (autoplay: none — it animates on its own internal clock, nothing for a synthetic-input driver to trigger). Three horizontal lanes are stacked evenly across the container's measured height (laneMargin = 0.14*H top/bottom), each running from a station box near the left edge (stationX = max(14, 0.1*W)) to a shared catch tray at the right (trayX = 0.78*W). Carrier size derives from the container's smaller dimension: carrierH = clamp(0.05*S, 4, 9)px, carrierW = 2.1*carrierH. Each lane runs its own independent cycle clock with a jittered period averaging DISPATCH_INTERVAL = 2600ms (+/-15%, re-rolled every cycle via Math.random on the live path / a seeded mulberry32 on the reduced-motion path) and a stagger offset of cycleLen/3 between lanes at start so all three are never in flight together. Within a cycle, elapsed ms since launch (0 at cycle start) drives one shared `lenFraction(elapsed)` function reused for every lane: 0-180ms eases in (quadratic) covering 0-18% of the tube length (launch, blower spool-up); 180-790ms advances linearly from 18% to 88% at constant velocity (cruise); 790-1050ms eases the remaining 88%->100% via a normalised exponential decay with a 70ms time constant (the trapped air-cushion braking against the carrier, a real dashpot curve, not a generic ease-out); past 1050ms the carrier is fully arrived, and for the following 90ms (to 1140ms) a small decaying `BOUNCE_PX=3` vertical oscillation (`3*exp(-4.5u)*cos(2*pi*1.6u)`) reads as the thunk settle. From 1140ms until the cycle wraps at its jittered period, the lane's carrier sits back at the station at 0.55 opacity (loaded, waiting for its next dispatch) rather than disappearing, so the diagram never shows an empty lane. The instant a lane's clock crosses 1050ms (arrival), a global deliveredCount increments and one of 6 tray-pip `<rect>` elements (round-robin by `(deliveredCount-1) % 6`, laid out 3 columns x 2 rows inside the tray outline) is marked filled and given a 220ms arrival flash: opacity eases from 1.0 down to its resting 0.55 via `1 - smoothstep(t/220)` added on top of the resting value — a pip that has never been filled stays at opacity 0 (present in the DOM, invisible), so early in a session the tray visibly builds up rather than starting full. On mount (and after every debounced 120ms ResizeObserver-triggered rebuild) a synchronous 21-second pre-roll runs the identical `advance()` step function in 16ms increments before the first paint, so the tray is never empty and at least one lane is never mid-launch at t0. Resting-loop check: t0 has some in-flight lane and some tray fill level; 2.5s later at least one full lane cycle's worth of arrival/relaunch has shifted both the flying carrier's position and the tray's fill/flash state (2.6s average cycle isn't commensurate with the 2.5s sample); 5s in, roughly two cycles have elapsed, both visibly different again — unforced, unbounded. REDUCED MOTION: `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` runs the same `advance()` step synchronously in 8ms increments with a seeded RNG until `deliveredCount` reaches 4 (roughly 3.5s of simulated time), then renders once with no rAF ever scheduled — freezing with the tray at a legible 4-of-6 mid-fill, one lane's carrier having just settled into place, and the other lanes independently mid-cruise or waiting at their stations, the single frame that shows tube, an in-flight carrier, a waiting carrier, and tray fill state all at once. Colors: tube channel is `var(--ns-muted)` at 0.4 opacity (a structural fill, not a separator, so it stays legible in light theme where `--border` alone would vanish); station and tray outlines are `var(--border)`, correctly used only as separators around otherwise-empty regions; carriers and tray pips are solid `var(--foreground)`, opacity-only in both themes, never accent-tinted. An optional hover-triggered readout (`showReadout`, default true) shows real derived state, "N in transit / M delivered" in `var(--ns-muted)`/`var(--foreground)` plain text — `inTransit` counts lanes with elapsed <= 1140ms (still visually animating), `delivered` is the running `deliveredCount`. `--ns-accent` is not used anywhere; there is no interaction chrome to color, and no focusable control (matches capstan-slip's precedent — a passive ambient status widget needs no Tab target). ResizeObserver rebuilds geometry and restarts the simulation (debounced 120ms) on any size change; IntersectionObserver pauses the rAF loop when off-screen and resumes it (fresh `last=0` so dt doesn't spike) when visible again; unmount cancels the rAF, disconnects both observers, and clears pending resize timers. DOM + SVG + CSS only, no canvas, zero dependencies.
